title: The JVP rule of `polynomial` returns a tangent of the shape of `x` if the constant coefficient broadcasts `x`
description: `lax.polynomial(x, coeffs)` broadcasts `x` and all coefficients against each other.
If only the constant coefficient `a_0` is larger than `x` along some axis, the primal is correct,
but the tangent with respect to `x` has the shape of `x` instead of the shape of the result.
Forward mode returns a tangent of the wrong shape, reverse mode raises a `ValueError`,
and `grad` of a sum silently returns a wrong value.
where `dy_dx = polynomial(x, deriv_coeffs)` has the shape of `x` and the coefficients of positive degree.
`a_0` does not occur in the derivative, so its shape is lost, and the tangent is never broadcast to the shape of the result.
The rule is correct if `a_0` broadcasts to the shape of `x` and the other coefficients, see `Jax.Lax.polynomialJvp_correct`.
The Lean model has no rank-0 arrays, so it refutes the rule for a linear coefficient of shape `(1,)`.
JAX behaves the same for the scalar coefficient `2.0` of the upstream issue.
reproducer: # The linear coefficient as an array of shape (1,), as in the Lean model, and as a scalar.
# Forward mode returns a tangent of shape (1,) instead of (3,).
# Reverse mode raises, because the cotangent has the shape of the result.
assert 'Expected cotangent type float32[1] but got float32[3]' in str(e), e
raise AssertionError('the cotangent has the right shape')
# The gradient of the sum is silently wrong: three outputs of slope 2 give 6, not 2.
